independent_node_reconstruction.finding: The Twilight Flayer node contributed 66 of 67 eligible healer-targeting samples. Route generation 1 contributed the remaining one sample; every other reconstructed node contributed zero eligible healer exposure. Overall retention still passed, so the failure is localized healer protection and dwell rather than global threat collapse.

movement_diagnostic.finding: The current handoff path was valid, moving, and making measurable progress. The stored recovery_result was historical state and is not evidence that the current MoveBotToPoint call failed.

control_flow_timeline.finding: Roar secured the 650-659 wave and created a new 2500 ms post-Roar remote-cluster reservation.
Continuation remained authoritative while the original wave became fully tank-owned; a new split wave began entering during the same reservation.
The active handoff had rebound to the new wave: five of 27 engaged identities targeted the healer while the Feral remained on a valid moving path.
Eight new-wave identities targeted the healer; GUID 647 began the 5619 ms maximum-dwell episode.
The prior bounded reservation expired and the ordinary selector immediately established another 2500 ms pre-Roar reservation for the same unresolved split wave.
Within 26 ms of the renewed reservation expiring, the selector established a third consecutive pre-Roar reservation instead of yielding one decision to the existing local threat resolver.
The first Roar against the new wave occurred 3546 ms after the maximum-dwell episode began, already beyond the strict 3000 ms dwell ceiling.
A second Roar reduced the split wave, but GUID 647 remained healer-owned through 1785680386977.
The existing single-target recovery cleared the final lingering identity after the chained handoff cycles ended.

hypotheses.name: rerun128_current_path_rejection_starvation
hypotheses.evidence: Rerun130 emitted continuation rather than path-rejected actions, and the immutable diagnostic showed active_path_valid=true, is_moving=true, 3.55092 yards of decision progress, and zero milliseconds since progress. LastRecoveryResult/recovery_result was stale historical state and cannot prove the current MoveBotToPoint return value.

hypotheses.name: bounded_handoff_rebind_and_immediate_reacquisition
hypotheses.evidence: A successful post-Roar reservation remained active as a new split wave appeared, rebound to new healer-owned identities, then was followed at 1785680381867 and again at 1785680384393 by fresh pre-Roar reservations immediately after expiry. Individually bounded 2500 ms reservations therefore formed a longer effective movement-ownership interval.

hypotheses.name: audit_scope_or_denominator_error
hypotheses.evidence: Independent identity-scoped reconstruction exactly matched 1775/1870 tank retention, 67/1870 healer exposure, and 5619 ms maximum per-hostile dwell under the unchanged 3000 ms acquisition grace.

hypotheses.name: missing_tank_threat_aura_or_cast_failure
hypotheses.evidence: Tank threat-aura uptime and active-action coverage were 1.0, 291 Feral attempts had a 0.0 cast-failure rate, and overall tank retention passed at 0.9492.

hypotheses.name: global_threat_multiplier_or_gate_relaxation_needed
hypotheses.evidence: The failure is localized to one Flayer split-wave handoff chain. Global threat inflation or acceptance relaxation would hide a real current-victim exposure episode.

accepted_causal_chain: A successful Roar created a nominally bounded 2500 ms post-Roar remote-cluster handoff while the original 650-659 wave became tank-owned.

A new 640-649 split wave appeared before that reservation fully yielded decision ownership, and secure-majority/cluster rebinding transferred the active handoff anchor to the new healer-owned identities.
The active path was valid and making real progress, so continuingRemotePath kept moved=true and the rerun128 false-return fallback correctly did not execute.
When the reservation expired, the ordinary remote-cluster selector immediately established another pre-Roar reservation; when that reservation expired, it established a third reservation 26 ms later.

Those individually bounded reservations formed a longer effective movement-ownership interval, delaying the first Roar against the new wave until 3546 ms after GUID 647's healer-targeting episode began.
Repeated continuation, movement, and Roar cycles retained 94.92 percent of all eligible hostile samples but left GUID 647 on the healer for 5619 ms and produced 67 eligible healer-target samples.
The strict identity-scoped role audit correctly passed tank retention and rejected healer exposure and dwell.
evidence_limitations: LastRecoveryResult and trace recovery_result persist historical path state and do not identify the current movement call's return value.

LastMovementProgressMs is refreshed by combat/casting paths and is not independently a movement-only signal; this diagnosis instead uses ActivePathValid, IsMoving, DistanceMovedSinceLastDecision, and the action branch outcome together.

The exact handoff-expiry transition is inferred from the immutable action timestamps and the compiled 2500 ms reservation contract because the trace does not serialize FeralHealerThreatHandoffUntilMs directly.
The evidence supports correcting reservation ownership and reacquisition; it does not support changing victim assignment, threat multipliers, route semantics, or audit thresholds.

smallest_safe_correction.scope: ordinary-trash Feral healer-threat handoff expiration and post-Roar remote-cluster movement only
smallest_safe_correction.change: Treat an expired handoff as a real yield boundary: clear it but prevent the ordinary remote-cluster selector from immediately creating another reservation in that decision, allowing the existing nearby Roar, Growl, or density resolver to own the decision. Keep the actual path-rejection fallback. Use the existing collision-safe Roar stand-off rather than the hostile's exact position when a successful Roar creates a post-Roar remote-cluster path.
uses_existing_evidence: existing local Demoralizing Roar, Growl, and density recovery
